evidence.Lateral Meniscus: Degenerative multidirectional tearing of the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus with a large radial oblique tear at the junction of the body and posterior horn.
evidence.Medial OA: There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning, which has progressed without full-thickness cartilage loss or reactive subchondral marrow changes. Marginal osteophytes are noted
evidence.Lateral OA: Severe chondropathy in the lateral compartment with full-thickness cartilage thinning, reactive subchondral marrow changes and osteophytes which have progressed.
evidence.PF OA: Mild cartilage thinning at the patellar medial and lateral facet as well as the trochlear surface, with a full-thickness cartilage fissure at the lateral patellar facet and mild reactive subchondral marrow changes. Marginal osteophytes also noted.
evidence.Effusion: Moderate to large knee joint effusion and popliteal cyst.
evidence.Baker's: popliteal cyst. The popliteal cyst measures 2.7 cm x 2.1 cm x 4.2 cm in length.
